newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ sees NZ$1 bln govt bond programme for 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: ANZ sees NZ$1 bln govt bond programme for 1997/98.

text.p: The strength of New Zealand's fiscal outlook, specifically the path of net public debt reduction, presents a significant risk to the ongoing issuance of government debt securities, ANZ Bank said on Wednesday.

"The expected reduction in net public debt over the coming year (around NZ$1.8 billion) should comfortably cover the remainder of the 7/97s outstanding in the market -- the only bond maturing in the 1997/98 fiscal year," ANZ said in a report.
"Consequently, at this stage there is no significant financing requirement to necessitate a programme of domestic debt issuance over the coming year."
However, ANZ said there were some considerations it felt would prompt the government to announce a limited bond tender programme for the 1997/98 fiscal year in its June 26 budget.

It said attempting to stop all bond issuance over the year could be problematic if the projected balance of cash flows proved weaker than expected (for example if tax flows slipped below forecast as ministers have been warning may happen).
"Consequently, announcing a bond programme would provide a measure of insurance," ANZ said.

The banks economists said there was an argument for the government to preserve the liquidity of key benchmark maturities, both as a contingency to ensure a ready market should debt financing be needed at some stage in the future, and to underpin the pricing of other New Zealand dollar securities.

Moreover, there was also a case for the government to lengthen the duration of its remaining outstanding liabilities in an attempt to match the long term nature of many of its assets, such as roads, dams and other public assets.

"While exact matching may be impractical (as it would involve issuing very long dated securities), the government is moving further away from this objective at present with the duration of the ordinary bond portfolio having fallen from around four years to close to 3.5 years over the past 18 months," ANZ said.
"This compares with an average five to six years for most AAA rated countries."
ANZ said while the Reserve Bank had not decided to pursue most of its proposals for altering monetary policy implementation and signalling, it was still considering discounting issuance of RB bills.

"If this were to occur, the $1.125 billion of RB bills outstanding would need to be replaced by either T-bills or bonds given that the expected reduction in net public debt over the coming year is unlikely to be able to absorb this after accounting for the remaining 7/97s and increases in assets (for example student loans)," ANZ said.

ANZ said the government may focus on reducing debt via T-bills rather than bonds. "There are currently more than $6 billion T-bills outstanding -- arguably an excessive quantity of short term funding for a government which has ben running operating surpluses for the past four years."
Given all of these factors, ANZ said it expected the government to announce a bond tender programme for the 1997/98 fiscal year of around $1.0 billion.

"This is likely to mainly comprise issuance of ordinary semi-annual coupon bonds, although we expect around $200-$300 million of inflation-indexed bonds (IIBs) to be included in this tender programme.
It said it expected most, if not all, of the $700-$800 million ordinary bond programme to comprise issuance of a new 2008 bond to lengthen the duration of the government bond curve.
ANZ said the balance of risks for the tender programme were on the downside. "There is a risk that the government could run an even smaller programme, or no programme at all," it said.
